subject: Post-demo: caching scenarios & effective $/1M token sensitivity
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Liu <cara@finoptics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: caching scenarios & effective $/1M token sensitivity

Hi Cara — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap + the two concrete asks we promised:

1) Our top-line takeaway from the demo: FinOptics' typical prompt patterns (short query + 2–3 sentence context) look well suited for a prefix/KV cache strategy. We believe a small amount of warm-state caching (1–2GB KV per model variant) can materially reduce token bill for the most frequent queries.

2) Next steps we agreed:
  - You: share a 2-week sample of anonymized query logs (headers + token counts) — procurement noted privacy constraints, happy to accept redacted logs.
  - Us: send a short model/hit-rate sensitivity workbook and a baseline effective $/1M tokens estimate under conservative/realistic/aggressive cache hit scenarios.

Attached: redwood-hitrate-models-aug18.csv (hit-rate scenarios + per-token math) and the recording link.

Key numbers (ballpark from today's settings):
  - Nominal list price (gptx-8k equivalent): $20 per 1M prompt+completions tokens (hosted).
  - No-cache effective: $20 / 1M tokens.
  - With 20% prefix hit (warm KV for reuse): effective price ≈ $16 / 1M tokens (~20% savings).
  - With 50% hit: effective price ≈ $12 / 1M tokens (~40% savings).
  - With aggressive strategy (70% hit on stable queries): effective price ≈ $8.5 / 1M tokens (~57% savings), but this assumes longer cache TTLs and more memory.

Assumptions listed in the CSV — we modeled prefix lengths, average completion length, and percent of tokens in cached prefix. I flagged two scenarios you asked us to prioritize: conservative (15–25% hit) and realistic (35–55% hit).

If useful, Ben and Marissa can run a quick scoped projection against the redacted logs once you share them; we can return a one-pager showing expected monthly spend at your forecasted volumes.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short email routing the internal ask.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-hitrate-models-aug18.csv (CSV, 14KB); demo-recording link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-demo-recording

Thanks Sean — this is helpful and aligns with what I took away. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- We can share 14 days of redacted logs (no PII, just query hash + prompt tokens + completion tokens + timestamp). Procurement asked that we avoid raw text in the export. Is that OK for your projection?
- Our current monthly token burn is roughly 70–90M tokens on the search assistant flow (spiky by hour). We were hoping to get to an effective price in the $10–12 / 1M tokens range given our budget target.

If you can run the realistic hit scenario (35–55%) against the redacted sample and show monthly spend at our current volumes, that should get us comfortable for the procurement review.

I’ll copy procurement on the export — sending separately.

—Cara
Cara Liu
Head of Product, FinOptics
cara@finoptics.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Cara Liu <cara@finoptics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: caching scenarios & effective $/1M token sensitivity

Perfect — redacted logs are exactly what we need. Quick clarification on the hit-rate modeling so procurement sees the assumptions up-front:

- What counts as a cache hit: exact prefix reuse within the TTL window (we model TTL in minutes).
- Conservative case: short TTLs (5–15 minutes), lower reuse across users — expect 15–25% prefix hits.
- Realistic case: 30–45 minute TTL, user query overlap in the search assistant — 35–55% prefix hits.
- Aggressive case: targeted user sessions + pre-warming for top-100 queries — 60–75% prefix hits (higher memory).

I’ve attached the CSV where each row is a volume bucket (10M / 50M / 100M tokens) with corresponding effective $/1M under each hit band. For your volumes (70–90M), the realistic band maps to roughly $9.5–$12.5 / 1M tokens in our model: that matches your procurement target window.

Action items for us once we get the redacted sample:
  1) Ben: run the sample through the hit-rate estimator and return a spreadsheet with bucketed monthly cost and confidence bands.
  2) Marissa: prepare a short procurement-friendly one-pager that lists assumptions (TTL, avg completion length, cache memory required) and a recommended Dedicated vs Hosted configuration for FinOptics.
  3) Sean (me): coordinate timing for a 30-minute handoff call with procurement to walk the numbers.

Cara — when procurement sends the export, please include an example of the top 200 distinct queries (hash + count) if possible — that helps prioritize pre-warming.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

—Sean

Forwarding the thread after a quick pass on the CSV — I ran an initial estimate against the conservative/realistic buckets and left inline notes in the attached redwood-hitrate-models-aug18.csv. Highlights: 

- Using FinOptics' stated volume (70–90M/month) and the realistic hit band (35–55%), our projections show median effective price ≈ $10.8 / 1M tokens (95% conf band $9.0–$12.4).
- Biggest sensitivity: average completion length — if completions average 120 tokens instead of 80, the effective price increases ~18% (more completions dilutes prefix savings).
- Memory trade: achieving >50% hit reliably requires 3–4GB KV per model + slightly higher warm-up logic; that still fits within Redwood Dedicated sizing for a single model variant.

Attachments: redwood-hitrate-models-aug18.csv (I added a tab with per-bucket tables), demo recording link as reference.

Recommended next internal steps:
  - Marissa to draft the procurement one-pager (assumptions + recommended config).
  - Ava to scope a short Dedicated cost comparison (commit tiers vs hosted rates) for the one-pager.
  - Sean to schedule the procurement handoff once Cara shares the redacted logs.

Ben
